title: Work and Jobs
description: Mendeskripsikan pekerjaan dan tempat kerja, menjelaskan cara orang bekerja dengan adverbs of manner, membicarakan keinginan dan kebutuhan dengan verb + to-infinitive, serta memakai much, many, a lot of, a little, dan a few.
objectives: Menggunakan kosakata pekerjaan, tempat kerja, dan kegiatan kerja
Membentuk dan memakai adverbs of manner (carefully, well, hard)
Menggunakan want to, need to, would like to, dan kata kerja lain + to-infinitive
Memilih much, many, a lot of, a little, atau a few dengan tepat

lessons.title: Jobs and Workplaces
lessons.summary: Kosakata pekerjaan, tempat kerja, dan kegiatan kerja serta cara menanyakan pekerjaan seseorang.
objectives: Menyebutkan pekerjaan, tempat kerja, dan tugas utamanya
Menanyakan dan menjelaskan pekerjaan: What do you do? I work as/in/for...
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Menanyakan pekerjaan
Pertanyaan paling umum adalah **What do you do?** (Apa pekerjaanmu?). Pertanyaan ini memakai present simple, jadi artinya *pekerjaan rutin*, bukan *sedang melakukan apa*.

| Pertanyaan | Jawaban |
| --- | --- |
| What do you do? | *I'm **a** nurse. / I'm **an** engineer.* |
| Where do you work? | *I work **in** a hospital. / I work **at** Sinar Bank.* |
| Who do you work for? | *I work **for** a small IT company.* |
| What does your job involve? | *I answer phone calls and help customers.* |

### Jangan lupa a/an
Dalam bahasa Inggris, pekerjaan **selalu** memakai *a/an* setelah *I'm / He's / She's*:
- ✗ *She is engineer.* → ✓ *She is **an** engineer.*

### Preposisi penting
- **work as** + pekerjaan: *I work **as** a receptionist.*
- **work in** + tempat/bidang: *in an office, in a hospital, in tourism*
- **work at** + tempat spesifik: *at the airport, at Green Valley Café*
- **work for** + perusahaan/orang: *for a bank, for my uncle*

### Pekerjaan, tempat, dan tugas
| Job | Workplace | What they do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chef | kitchen, restaurant | cooks meals |
| nurse | hospital, clinic | looks after patients |
| mechanic | garage | repairs cars |
| receptionist | hotel, office | welcomes visitors, answers the phone |
| accountant | office | manages money and taxes |
| architect | office | designs buildings |
| farmer | farm | grows food, keeps animals |
| shop assistant | shop | serves customers |
| pilot | plane, airport | flies planes |
| factory worker | factory | makes products |

### Kata kerja tugas
*serve customers* (melayani pelanggan), *repair* (memperbaiki), *design* (merancang), *look after* (merawat), *manage* (mengelola), *deal with problems* (menangani masalah).

lessons.title: Adverbs of Manner: Carefully, Well, Hard
lessons.summary: Menjelaskan cara seseorang melakukan sesuatu dengan adverbs of manner.
objectives: Membentuk adverb of manner dari adjective (+ -ly)
Menggunakan adverb tidak beraturan: well, fast, hard, late
Meletakkan adverb pada posisi yang benar
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Adjective vs adverb
- **Adjective** menjelaskan **kata benda** (orang/benda): *She is a **careful** driver.* (pengemudi yang hati-hati)
- **Adverb of manner** menjelaskan **kata kerja** — *bagaimana* sesuatu dilakukan: *She drives **carefully**.* (menyetir dengan hati-hati)

Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering memakai *dengan* + adjective (*dengan hati-hati, dengan cepat*). Dalam bahasa Inggris, adjective berubah menjadi adverb.

### Pembentukan
| Aturan | Contoh |
| --- | --- |
| adjective + **-ly** | quick → quick**ly**, slow → slow**ly**, careful → careful**ly**, quiet → quiet**ly** |
| konsonan + **y** → **-ily** | easy → eas**ily**, happy → happ**ily**, angry → angr**ily** |
| **-le** → **-ly** | gentle → gent**ly**, terrible → terrib**ly** |

### Adverb tidak beraturan
| Adjective | Adverb | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| good | **well** | *He speaks English **well**.* |
| fast | **fast** | *She types **fast**.* |
| hard | **hard** | *They work **hard**.* |
| late | **late** | *The train arrived **late**.* |
| early | **early** | *I got up **early**.* |

**Hati-hati:** *hardly* **bukan** adverb dari *hard*. *Hardly* berarti *hampir tidak*: *I hardly slept.* (Saya hampir tidak tidur.) Begitu juga ✗ *fastly* tidak ada.

### Posisi adverb
Adverb of manner biasanya diletakkan **setelah kata kerja** atau **setelah objek**:
- *She speaks **quietly**.* (setelah kata kerja)
- *He finished the report **quickly**.* (setelah objek)

Jangan letakkan di antara kata kerja dan objek: ✗ *She speaks **well** English.* ✓ *She speaks English **well**.*

### Dengan very / really
Kamu bisa menambahkan *very* atau *really*: *He works **very hard**. She sings **really beautifully**.*

### Kata kerja be, look, feel
Setelah *be, look, feel, seem*, gunakan **adjective**, bukan adverb: *You look **tired**. The food tastes **good**.* (✗ *looks tiredly*)

lessons.title: Want To, Need To, Would Like To
lessons.summary: Kata kerja yang diikuti to-infinitive untuk membicarakan keinginan, kebutuhan, dan rencana.
objectives: Menggunakan want, need, would like, hope, plan, decide, learn + to + base verb
Membedakan verb + to-infinitive dan verb + -ing (like, enjoy)
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Verb + to + base verb
Beberapa kata kerja harus diikuti **to + bentuk dasar** (*to-infinitive*) jika ada kata kerja kedua.

*I **want to find** a new job.* (Saya ingin mencari pekerjaan baru.)

| Kata kerja | Arti | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **want to** | ingin | *I want to work abroad.* |
| **need to** | perlu | *We need to finish this today.* |
| **would like to** ('d like to) | ingin (lebih sopan) | *I'd like to speak to the manager.* |
| **hope to** | berharap | *She hopes to get a promotion.* |
| **plan to** | berencana | *They plan to open a new branch.* |
| **decide to** | memutuskan | *He decided to change jobs.* |
| **learn to** | belajar (keterampilan) | *I learned to drive last year.* |
| **try to** | berusaha | *Try to arrive on time.* |

### Bentuk negatif dan pertanyaan
Untuk kata kerja biasa seperti *want* dan *need*, gunakan **do/does/did**:
- *I **don't want to** work at night.*
- ***Does** she **need to** wear a uniform?*
- *He **didn't plan to** stay so long.*

### Would like to vs want to
**Would like to** artinya sama dengan *want to*, tetapi **lebih sopan**. Sangat cocok untuk wawancara kerja dan situasi formal:
- *I want to see the manager.* (terdengar menuntut)
- *I'**d like to** see the manager, please.* (sopan)

Bentuk singkat: *I'd, you'd, she'd, we'd, they'd*. Negatif: *I wouldn't like to...*

### Like + -ing vs would like to
| like + -ing (A1) | would like to |
| --- | --- |
| kesukaan umum | keinginan tertentu |
| *I **like working** with people.* | *I'**d like to work** in a hotel one day.* |

Kata kerja lain yang diikuti **-ing**: *enjoy, love, hate, finish*. ✓ *I enjoy working here.* ✗ *I enjoy to work here.*

### Kesalahan umum
- Lupa *to*: ✗ *I want work.* → ✓ *I want **to** work.*
- Memakai -ing: ✗ *I need finishing.* → ✓ *I need **to finish**.*
- *to* + bentuk lampau: ✗ *He decided to changed.* → ✓ *He decided **to change**.*

lessons.title: Much, Many, A Lot Of, A Little, A Few
lessons.summary: Menyatakan jumlah dengan quantifier untuk kata benda terhitung dan tak terhitung.
objectives: Menggunakan much/many dalam kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan
Menggunakan a lot of, a little, dan a few dengan tepat
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Ingat: countable dan uncountable
Di A1 kamu belajar bahwa kata benda ada yang **terhitung** (*countable*: a job, two emails, three colleagues) dan **tak terhitung** (*uncountable*: work, money, time, information, advice, experience). Quantifier yang dipakai tergantung jenis kata bendanya.

### Tabel quantifier
| Arti | Countable (jamak) | Uncountable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| banyak | **many** / **a lot of** | **much** / **a lot of** |
| sedikit (tapi ada) | **a few** | **a little** |
| berapa banyak? | **How many**...? | **How much**...? |

### Much dan many
**Much** dan **many** paling sering dipakai dalam **kalimat negatif** dan **pertanyaan**:
- *We don't have **much** time.* (uncountable)
- *Are there **many** jobs in your town?* (countable)
- *How **many** people work here?*

Dalam kalimat **positif**, penutur asli biasanya memakai **a lot of**:
- *She has **a lot of** experience.* (lebih alami daripada *She has much experience*)
- *There are **a lot of** emails in my inbox.*

### A few dan a little
Keduanya berarti **sedikit, tetapi cukup/ada** (makna positif):
- *I have **a few** questions.* (beberapa pertanyaan — countable)
- *There's **a little** coffee left.* (sedikit kopi — uncountable)

### Kata benda tak terhitung yang sering salah
Kata-kata ini **uncountable** dalam bahasa Inggris, walaupun dalam bahasa Indonesia terasa bisa dihitung:
*information, advice, work, homework, money, equipment, furniture, news*.
- ✗ *many informations* → ✓ *a lot of information*
- ✗ *two advices* → ✓ *two pieces of advice*

### Too much / too many
*Too* berarti *terlalu*: *I have **too much** work and **too many** meetings this week!*

### Ringkasan cepat
- Bisa diberi angka? → **many / a few**
- Tidak bisa diberi angka? → **much / a little**
- Kalimat positif, banyak? → **a lot of** (keduanya)

lessons.title: Describing Your Job and Work Preferences
lessons.summary: Mendeskripsikan pekerjaan, kondisi kerja, dan preferensi kerja.
objectives: Menggunakan kosakata kondisi kerja: salary, colleague, part-time, shift
Mendeskripsikan pekerjaan dan preferensi kerja dengan semua tata bahasa unit ini
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi, coba latihan berbicara, dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Kosakata kondisi kerja
| English | Indonesia |
| --- | --- |
| salary | gaji (bulanan) |
| colleague | rekan kerja |
| boss / manager | atasan / manajer |
| full-time / part-time | penuh waktu / paruh waktu |
| shift (night shift) | giliran kerja (shift malam) |
| work from home | bekerja dari rumah |
| well-paid / badly paid | bergaji tinggi / bergaji rendah |
| stressful | penuh tekanan |
| rewarding | memuaskan, bermakna |
| apply for a job | melamar pekerjaan |
| job interview | wawancara kerja |

### Mendeskripsikan pekerjaan
Gabungkan semua tata bahasa unit ini:

*I'm a nurse. I work **in** a big hospital in Semarang. I work **long shifts** and sometimes I have to work at night. The job is **stressful**, but it's very **rewarding** because I help **a lot of** people. My colleagues are friendly and they work very **hard**. In the future, I'**d like to** become a head nurse, so I **need to** study more.*

| Bagian | Tata bahasa |
| --- | --- |
| Pekerjaan dan tempat | I'm a/an..., I work in/at/for... |
| Tugas | present simple: I look after patients |
| Kondisi | adjectives: stressful, well-paid |
| Cara bekerja | adverbs: carefully, hard |
| Jumlah | a lot of, a few, much, many |
| Rencana dan keinginan | want to, would like to, need to, hope to |

### Membicarakan preferensi kerja
- *I **like working** with people.* / *I **don't like working** alone.*
- *I **enjoy** solving problems.*
- *I'**d like to work** from home two days a week.*
- *I **don't want to work** night shifts.*
- *I **prefer** working outdoors.* (prefer + -ing = lebih suka)

### Pertanyaan wawancara kerja sederhana
- *Why do you want to work here?*
- *How much experience do you have?*
- *Can you work on weekends?*
- *What do you want to do in five years?*

Jawab dengan kalimat lengkap dan berikan alasan dengan **because**.

questions.prompt: Describe your job (or your dream job) for 45–60 seconds. Say where you work, what you do, what is good and bad about the job, and what you would like to do in the future.
questions.sampleAnswer: I work as a receptionist at a hotel in Yogyakarta. I welcome guests, answer the phone and deal with problems. I work full-time, and sometimes I have to work the night shift. The salary isn't very high, but I meet a lot of interesting people, and my colleagues are friendly. I speak English well, but I need to learn a little Japanese because we have many Japanese guests. In the future, I'd like to become a hotel manager.
questions.explanation: Gunakan work as/in, present simple untuk tugas, adjectives untuk kondisi, quantifiers, dan would like to / need to untuk rencana.

questions.prompt: Read the job advert. Which sentence is true?
questions.context:
**Part-time waiter needed — Green Valley Café**
We are looking for a friendly waiter to work three evenings a week (Thursday to Saturday, 5–10 p.m.). You don't need much experience, but you need to speak English well. Free meals for staff. To apply, send an email to jobs@greenvalley.example by 30 June.
options: The job is only on three evenings a week.
You need a lot of experience.
Staff have to pay for their meals.
You can apply until the end of July.
questions.explanation: Iklan: three evenings a week. Tidak perlu banyak pengalaman, makan gratis, dan batas lamaran 30 Juni.

questions.explanation: Menjelaskan cara memeriksa → adverb carefully. Would like dan need diikuti to + base verb.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct word: Our boss speaks very ___, so it's hard to hear him in meetings.
Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.text: Our company is growing fast. We need ___ (hire) two more drivers.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Need + to + base verb: need to hire.

unitTestQuestions.text: There are ___ applicants for the job, but only ___ of them have experience.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Applicants terhitung dalam kalimat positif → a lot of. Hanya sedikit dari mereka (terhitung) → a few.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Adverb dari hard adalah hard. Hardly berarti hampir tidak.

answers: I would like to work in a hospital.
